S18.01.note: The evidence line apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1243 no longer holds the feature. The title is set in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts (title: text.trim().slice(0, 80) || 'Developer session'). Not a title generated by a model, and I did not confirm the row text in the Sessions sheet.
steps: Sign in, open the AGI Code panel and send a first message in a new chat.
Click the Sessions button (title "Sessions") in the panel header.
Compare: the new session's row shows the start of your first message (cut at 80 characters), not a blank row. An empty first message gets the fallback title "Developer session".
S18.01.where: No control of its own. Seen in the Sessions list: the Sessions button in the AGI Code panel header (title "Sessions")

S18.04.note: Archive has no button in the panel; it is only in the Command Palette. Restore is a button in the archived list.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Archive Conversation".
Pick the session to archive, then click "Archive" in the modal warning.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Archived Sessions" (or click the Archived sessions button in the Sessions sheet).
Select the archived session and click the Restore button (tooltip "Restore"), then compare: the session is back in the normal Sessions list and was not lost.
S18.04.where: Command Palette > Code: Archive Conversation (archive). Restore: Sessions button > Archived sessions, or Command Palette > Code: Show Sessions History > Archived sessions

S18.05.needs: a session to delete (archive it first to test the archived route)
S18.05.note: Both routes ask for confirmation. Whether it disappears from every AGI surface is not checked in the code I read.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Permanently Delete Conversation".
Pick the session to delete.
Read the modal warning and click "Delete Permanently".
Compare: the session is gone from the Sessions list and from the Archived sessions list.
S18.05.where: Command Palette > Code: Permanently Delete Conversation. Or Sessions button > Archived sessions > trash button (tooltip "Delete permanently")

S18.06.note: The visible word is Fork, not Duplicate. Whether the copy is fully independent was not checked in this code.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Fork Conversation".
Pick the session to copy.
Keep the suggested name "<session title> (fork)" or type a new one, then press Enter.
Compare: a new session opens with the copied history, and the original session is unchanged.
S18.06.where: Command Palette > Code: Fork Conversation (the app says Fork, not Duplicate)

S18.09.needs: a session that can send messages
S18.09.note: The modes are Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions, not chat/agent/work/plan. The command reads and writes the Config.agentMode setting, so I could not confirm that it is scoped to one conversation.
steps: Open a session and send one message in the current mode.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Set Agent Mode".
Pick a different mode, for example "Plan".
Send another message and compare: the reply follows the new mode (for example, plans first instead of editing).
S18.09.where: Command Palette > Code: Set Agent Mode, then pick Ask, Auto, Plan or Bypass permissions

labels.text: Copy a link to this session

S18.21.needs: a session that has messages, opened in the panel
S18.21.note: Expected lists message count and id. The receipt shows no message count, and the id appears only inside the copied link. Session Status shows the ID with a copy row.
steps: Open a session that has messages.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Session Activity".
Read the list under "Details": Model, Folder, Branch, Trust mode, and "Started from ... last active ...".
Compare with Expected: the created and updated times, model, project and a link ("Copy a link to this session") are there. Message count is not shown.
S18.21.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Session Activity (quick pick titled "Code, Session: <title>"). Also Command Palette > Code: Session Status for model, mode and context

S18.22.needs: a session with at least one file in context
S18.22.note: The context quick pick is built from the context panel provider. I did not confirm that it lists instructions or memory, which Expected mentions.
steps: Open a session and attach or use a file in it.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Context Files".
Read the list placeholder "Files in this conversation’s context…" and the files listed.

Run "Code: Session Status" and read the "Context" row: "X of Y tokens (Z%)" or "Not measured yet in this window". Compare with Expected: files and token use are shown. Instructions and memory are not confirmed.
S18.22.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Context Files (quick pick titled "Code, Context"). Also Command Palette > Code: Session Status > Context row (token count)

S18.23.needs: a signed-in account to see billed credits
S18.23.note: The breakdown is for this editor session across all models, not for one conversation, so Expected (per conversation) is not what the code shows. Plan usage is in Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage.
steps: Send a few messages in one or more sessions.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Token Breakdown".
Read the quick pick titled "Code -- Token Usage Breakdown": Input Tokens, Output Tokens, Estimated Credits, Billed Credits, Turns.
Compare: the counts rise with use. A message appears if nothing is measured yet.
S18.23.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Token Breakdown (also opened from the token count in the status bar)

S18.28.needs: a phone with the AGI Mobile app signed into the same account; a trusted folder open in VS Code
S18.28.note: Remote Control pairs a phone; the cloud route is a separate continue action. The owner's notes say Remote Control is hidden in v1 for mobile, which I did not check in this code.
steps: Open this folder in VS Code, trust it, and sign in.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Remote Control". Read the pairing QR code and pairing code.
On the phone, open the AGI Mobile app and choose "Pair with Desktop" (wording from the app's text, not verified on the phone).
Start a session in VS Code, then check that the same session shows on the phone and can be continued there. Compare with Expected.
S18.28.where: Command Palette > Code: Remote Control (pairs a phone; the phone then follows this window's sessions). Also Command Palette > Code: Continue in the Cloud, and the Sessions sheet button "Continue in the cloud"
